findings.title: `updateDevice` reassigns the captured `args` slice inside the session closure, so a retry would prepend the query twice
findings.description: Inside `updateDevice`, the closure passed to `s.sqlStore.WithDbSession` runs `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`. That reassigns the variable captured from the enclosing function, so the query is prepended to the outer `args` on every invocation of the closure. The closure runs once on the normal path, so this is latent, but any retry of the session callback would build `[query, query, ...]` and fail. Building the slice once outside the closure, or using a local variable inside it, avoids the problem.

findings.title: Zero rows affected is always reported as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which misstates the cause and can deny login for existing devices
findings.description: `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever `rowsAffected == 0`. That case also occurs when the device does not exist, or when its stored `updated_at` falls outside the `BETWEEN` window (more than 30 days old). In the window case the device is already known but is rejected. `Authenticate` in `client.go` treats `ErrDeviceLimitReached` as fatal and returns `nil, err`, so a returning anonymous device whose record is older than the window is locked out with a misleading "limit reached" error. The test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only covers the not-found case, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Several identifiers referenced in the changed code are outside the shown hunks and could not be checked
findings.description: Without file access I could not confirm these: `CountDevices` exists on `AnonDBStore` with the signature used in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`; `fmt` and `sqlstore` are imported in `database.go`; `anonstore` is still referenced in `impl_test.go` after the `anonDBStore` variable was removed (otherwise the import is unused); `time` is not used elsewhere in `client.go` after its import was removed; and `timeoutTag` has no other references. Each should be confirmed with a compile or a targeted read.
